evidence.scenario: Terminal failure classification preserves a typed cause chain and the real source stage, and a generic error carrying schema, validation or contract wording is not misclassified.
evidence.pass_criteria: Typed provider, timeout, connection, HTTP and data-gap failures resolve to distinct closed causes; only a safe message reaches the public result; the targeted suites exit 0.
evidence.actual_result: Two supplemental verification commands exited 0. The failure-classifier suite reported 21 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The job-lifecycle suite reported 13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Source review confirmed typed diagnostic construction carrying stage and subcause in the job module, and that only the safe message is placed on the terminal envelope.
evidence.validation_method: Static source-invariant review plus targeted offline pytest suites in an isolated detached worktree at the tested baseline.
limitations: Mock provider, in-memory job store and noop audit sink were used, so this item is S-class only and does not substitute for R, O or C.
No approved isolated command set exists in the repository; the commands are supplemental verification commands selected by the executor.

evidence.scenario: The canonical execution-spec hash and version are deterministic and are carried unchanged from parse through durable job admission.
evidence.pass_criteria: The canonical digest is a deterministic canonical serialisation, and the stored job records the same spec version and spec hash that the parse issued.
evidence.actual_result: One supplemental verification command exited 0 with 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Source review confirmed the canonical digest computes a SHA-256 over a sorted, separator-fixed JSON serialisation of the canonical rule, and the tests assert the stored execution spec version and hash equal the parse-issued values.
evidence.validation_method: Static source-invariant review plus targeted offline pytest node identifiers in an isolated detached worktree at the tested baseline.
limitations: Mock provider, in-memory job store and noop audit sink were used, so this item is S-class only.
Hash propagation into a real durable store is covered by the R item, not by this item.

evidence.scenario: A client-tampered execution spec is rejected before any job, outbox or runner side effect occurs.
evidence.pass_criteria: The request is refused with a typed conflict reason, and no job row and no runner invocation are produced.
evidence.actual_result: One supplemental verification command exited 0 with 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The tests assert an HTTP 409 response, a draft rule mismatch reason code, an empty job store and an empty runner call list. Source review confirmed the spec-hash comparison precedes quota consumption and durable admission, and that token forgery raises a typed draft token validation error on the same path.
evidence.validation_method: Static source-invariant review plus targeted offline pytest node identifiers in an isolated detached worktree at the tested baseline.
limitations: Mock provider, in-memory job store and noop audit sink were used, so this item is S-class only.
Absence of an audit side effect was observed through in-memory test doubles, not against a durable audit sink.

evidence.scenario: A clarification parse outcome stays non-executable and cannot be promoted into a canonical create request.
evidence.pass_criteria: Clarification drafts issue no execution spec, spec version, spec hash or parse token, and offer at most three explained choices.
evidence.actual_result: One supplemental verification command exited 0 with 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Source review confirmed the rule draft model validator rejects executable drafts that carry clarification choices and rejects clarification drafts that carry any execution spec or token, and that the clarification list is bounded at three entries.
evidence.validation_method: Static source-invariant review plus targeted offline pytest node identifiers in an isolated detached worktree at the tested baseline.
limitations: Mock provider, in-memory job store and noop audit sink were used, so this item is S-class only.
Clarification wording quality was not evaluated; only the structural non-executability contract was.

evidence.scenario: Against a disposable PostgreSQL database with the full migration set applied, concurrent parse-bound admission is atomic, migration-backed and race-safe, and an expired outbox lease is recoverable.
evidence.pass_criteria: Exactly one job, one idempotency record and one outbox row exist after two concurrent admissions; only one admission reports created; the raw natural-language input is absent from the stored job document; restart reconciliation preserves the queued outbox dispatch; an expired lease is reclaimed under the same outbox identifier and then settles.
evidence.actual_result: One supplemental verification command exited 0 with 1 passed, 0 failed and 0 skipped, executed against a real disposable PostgreSQL 16 instance rather than a test double. Transaction: the test asserts the job, idempotency and outbox row counts are exactly one each and that the raw query text is absent from the stored job document. Migration: the harness applies every service database migration, including the parse-bound admission migration, to a freshly created schema before exercising it. Race: two concurrent admissions on a thread pool yield exactly one created flag set true and a single job identifier, and after the outbox claim timestamp is aged the same outbox identifier is reclaimed, then settled and no longer claimable. Post-run inspection of the disposable database showed the migration-created analysis job, idempotency and outbox tables present with one row each.
evidence.validation_method: Isolated disposable PostgreSQL integration test executed from a detached worktree at the tested baseline, with shared and production database environment variables unset.
limitations: The database was a loopback-bound, auto-removed, memory-backed disposable container created solely for this run; it is not an operational or staging environment and this item is not promoted to O.
Concurrency was exercised with two threads inside a single process, so this item does not establish cross-process containment and is not promoted to C.
The single-process restart reconciliation observed here is R-level evidence only.

evidence.scenario: A restart across multiple worker processes reclaims interrupted work and reaps descendant processes without duplicating execution.
evidence.pass_criteria: Cross-process restart preserves exactly one durable job and one immutable terminal result, and descendant processes are cleaned up.
evidence.actual_result: Not satisfied; partial evidence only. Single-process restart reconciliation was observed against real PostgreSQL under the R item, where reconciliation reaped no jobs and preserved the queued outbox dispatch, and further reconciliation behaviour was exercised at S level with 11 passed against an in-memory store. Neither observation establishes multi-process worker containment or descendant cleanup, so this axis is not satisfied.
evidence.validation_method: Multi-process worker restart and descendant cleanup in an authorized isolated environment.
limitations: The single-process PostgreSQL reconciliation evidence is R-level and is explicitly not promoted to C.
The in-memory reconciliation suite is S-level only under the mock, memory and noop rule.
